objective: Blind-test baseline: how well a deterministic mapping pipeline (BioSample raw text -> ZOOMA -> ontology term) reproduces cMD3 human curation for body_site (UBERON) and disease (MONDO).

zooma_confidence_ladder: unfiltered, keep only target-ontology IRIs; tier HIGH
method.ambiguity_rule: winning tier contains >1 distinct target-ontology term -> ambiguous (top-ranked term kept as prediction)
method.healthy_rule: MONDO has no 'healthy' term: raw disease values normalizing to healthy/normal/control/none are mapped to pseudo-label 'healthy' by rule
method.disease_text_fallback: if the sample has no disease-ish attribute, the project title (<=300 chars) is used as disease text; per-sample source recorded
method.agreement_definition: ontology-ID match OR case/underscore-normalized label match; multi-part gold ('A;B') matches if any part matches
method.rate_denominator: n_with_raw_text = rows where raw candidate text existed; agreement/no-hit/ambiguous/mismatch rates partition this denominator; coverage losses (no_raw_field, fetch_error) reported separately
method.politeness: seqout sleep 2.6 s; ZOOMA/OLS4 sleep 0.35/0.3 s; all responses disk-cached

sampling.universe: seed_runs rows with cMD3 in seed_sources_all, non-empty sample_accession, non-null disease (9,053 of 32,042 cMD3 rows; alias-keyed rows lack accessions)

stratification.rule: 1 row per distinct non-healthy disease (99), filled to 150 with a 2nd row from random diseases; 150 healthy

sampling.gold: cMD3 body_site / disease free-text as registered in seed_copy (isolated copy of seed_registry.sqlite)

observations.note: coverage audit of the 300 raw seqout payloads; not part of the mapping pipeline — quantifies where disease text actually lives

disease.raw_text: Metagenomic analysis of fecal microbiome as a tool towards targeted non-invasive biomarkers for colorectal cancer
Longitudinal Stool Study of patients with IBD and controls
Metagenomic analysis of fecal microbiome as a tool towards targeted non-invasive biomarkers for colorectal cancer

caveats: cMD3 gold is already human-normalized vocabulary (e.g. 'feces', 'Colorectal Carcinoma'), while the pipeline starts from raw submitter free text ('G_DNA_Stool', 'stool sample'); disagreement therefore conflates ontology-mapping error with raw-text noise.
Sampling restricted to rows with a BioSample/Sample accession (9,053/32,042 cMD3 rows); alias-keyed rows could not be fetched.
body_site gold in the registry carries no UBERON IDs (body_site_uberon is NULL); gold was normalized via OLS4 exact label search at scoring time.
'Healthy' has no MONDO term; both gold and prediction rely on a keyword rule, so healthy agreement is partly by construction.

body_site mismatches are dominated by granularity, not error: raw sub-site text ('saliva', 'tongue dorsum', 'posterior fornix') maps to a precise UBERON term while cMD3 keeps coarse buckets ('oral cavity', 'vagina'); ID/label equality cannot see this containment.

BioSample attributes essentially never carry disease in this sample (see observations.disease_attr_present); the only deterministic disease route left is the study-level project title, which (a) ZOOMA mostly cannot map (long sentences) and (b) mispredicts controls inside case/control studies by construction.

MONDO label/synonym variance (e.g. 'colorectal carcinoma' vs 'colorectal cancer', cMD3 'Parasite Present' vs MONDO 'intestinal helminthiasis') makes some matches look like mismatches under strict ID-or-label equality.
ZOOMA GOOD-tier singletons were accepted; stricter HIGH-only settings trade no-hit rate for precision.
